messages.content: Help me generate the XContent with xContentBuilderInstance for a RootObjectMapper that includes default settings for dynamic date formats, dynamic templates, date detection, and numeric detection, while skipping runtime fields?

function.name: RootObjectMapper_doXContent
function.description: Serializes the RootObjectMapper settings to XContent, with options to include default values and to skip runtime fields. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

builder.description: The XContentBuilder to which the content should be written. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

params.description: Parameters controlling the serialization, including whether to include defaults and whether to skip runtime fields. This is Java ArrayList type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type any; they are not in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function RootObjectMapper_doXContent with builder and params. We need to provide builder as string representation of XContentBuilder instance. And params as string representation of ArrayList containing options: include defaults, skip runtime fields. Also we need to set dynamic date formats, dynamic templates, date detection, numeric detection. But the function only serializes settings; we need to set those on RootObjectMapper before calling. But we can't modify RootObjectMapper here. We just need to call function with appropriate parameters. Provide builder string "xContentBuilderInstance". Params string representation of ArrayList with options: include defaults true, skip runtime fields true. Also maybe include dynamic date formats etc. But those are part of RootObjectMapper settings. We assume they are already set. So we just call function.

Thus output: call to functions.RootObjectMapper_doXContent with builder: "xContentBuilderInstance" and params: "[includeDefaults:true, skipRuntimeFields:true]". Use JSON-like string? The function expects string representation of Java ArrayList type parameter in string representation. So we can provide something like "[true, true]"? But we need to specify which options. Let's assume the array contains two booleans: includeDefaults and skipRuntimeFields. So we pass "[true, true]".

Thus answer: call function.
